CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up of chronic problems.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Anna is a 44-year-old female with a past medical history significant for arthritis, gout, and reflux who presents today for follow-up of her chronic problems. She was last seen approximately six months ago. Regarding her arthritis, she reports improvement with exercise including pilates and weightlifting, which has helped build muscle strength. She has recovered well with physical therapy for her right knee and is now able to walk 1 to 1.5 miles per day. She had an episode of gout affecting her right first metatarsophalangeal joint approximately two months ago, which resolved with medication. She is taking allopurinol as prescribed with no further flare-ups. For her reflux, she was started on omeprazole and has attempted dietary modifications, but has not completely eliminated problematic foods. She continues to experience episodes with nausea and actual vomiting in the mornings. She reports associated abdominal pain and bloating. She denies diarrhea and weight loss. Last bowel movement was two days ago, which was normal with no blood.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and abdominal distension. Denies diarrhea, weight loss, fever, and chills.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Arthritis, gout, reflux.

MEDICATIONS
Omeprazole 40 mg once daily, allopurinol 100 mg once daily.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not documented.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs are good. Cardiovascular: heart sounds normal. Pulmonary: lungs sound normal. Abdomen: tenderness to palpation in the right upper quadrant without rebound, guarding, or peritoneal signs. Right knee: mild effusion, slight pain to palpation, and decreased range of motion.

RESULTS
Autoimmune panel: unremarkable. Right knee x-ray: no fracture, residual arthritis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Reflux with nausea and vomiting: Continue omeprazole 40 mg once daily and continue dietary modifications. Obtain right upper quadrant ultrasound to rule out gallstones. Check labs.
2. Gout: Continue allopurinol 100 mg once daily. Refill ordered.
3. Arthritis, right knee: Continue pilates and use of knee. Patient encouraged to follow up if any issues arise, at which time further imaging or intervention can be discussed.
